title: Maha Shivaratri as a night curriculum
word: Maha Shivaratri as a night curriculum
hook: gray light over the temple roof, one last worship, and food handed to someone else before the fast is broken
carry: Maha Shivaratri as a night curriculum

segments.voice: Yesterday, in Maha Shivaratri as a night curriculum, the offering: water, bilva, a wild flower, small so the care can be large. Today the night ends, and so does this part of the path.

The sky over the temple roof goes from black to slate to a thin gray. Birds start before anyone else. People who have been up all night stand, stretch, wince, and gather for one last round of worship. The bell rings. The lamp is waved. Then a woman near the gate unties a cloth bundle she's carried since yesterday. There's food inside, and she has fasted a full day. She hands it out first, to the people beside her, to the man sweeping the steps. Only then does she take a bite.
screen: `BLACK, SLATE, GRAY.` → `ONE LAST WORSHIP.` → `FOOD HANDED OUT FIRST.`

segments.voice: Breaking a fast at the right time is called parana. In the Shiva Purana's account of the vow, the night doesn't end with the last song. The next morning brings worship again, and giving, and only then is the fast broken. The vow closes the way it opened, on purpose. That ending matters. A night like this can turn into a story you tell about yourself: I stayed up, I didn't eat. The morning undoes that. It sends you back to ordinary things, food, a tired body, other people's hunger, and asks you to bring the night with you. If the night was about attention, the morning is where it's tested. The whole course: a resolve, a fast, a vigil, a name, an offering, and a morning that hands the night back to ordinary life. It closes the Shiva part of the path too. We read selections of the Shiva Purana: the pillar no one could measure, Sati who would not hear him mocked, Parvati's tapas. We stood before Nataraja, the dancer, walked through the Shiva Sahasranama, opened Kashmir Shaivism through the Shiva Sutras, lived inside the Rudram, and kept one great night. Tomorrow the path turns from a god to a way of thinking: the six darshanas, schools of Hindu thought, set side by side and never ranked. First, Nyaya, the school of logic.
screen: `PARANA: BREAKING THE FAST.` · `WORSHIP, GIVING, THEN FOOD.` · `THE MORNING TESTS THE NIGHT.` · `THE SHIVA PART, GATHERED UP.` · then, large: `BRING THE NIGHT WITH YOU.`

segments.voice: Sit as if the night has just ended and the light is coming up, and walk back slowly through its lessons: the resolve, the fast, the vigil, the name, the offering. Hold the one that stayed with you, and let it go with you into the first ordinary thing you'll do after this sit. If you pray, you can give thanks to Shiva, or to the God you know, for the night.
Maha Shivaratri as a night curriculum. The last lesson: parana, the morning, when worship and giving come first and the fast is broken.
